prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1364; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a two-vehicle collision at an intersection in Baytown, Texas, where a vehicle driven by Driver 1 was struck on the driver's side by a vehicle driven by Driver 2. Driver 1 reported neck and lower back strain and said the impact pushed the vehicle sideways into the curb. Driver 1's Passenger was present in the vehicle at the time of the collision, and officers and other people on scene confirmed this. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy for the vehicle. Officers observed no earlier damage to the vehicle, and Driver 1 did not report any prior incidents affecting it. The side damage is consistent with a side impact of this type, and the reported back strain is a plausible injury for a crash of this kind. However, no independent witnesses came forward, no photographs of the scene were submitted, and no other report of the collision was located. Officers were not able to determine whether all of the visible damage resulted from this impact alone. The collision is documented based on the statements of those involved and on the physical evidence observed at the scene.
